question: What is the primary purpose of inserting an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To secure and maintain a patent airway
options.B: To measure systemic blood pressure continuously
options.C: To prevent the stomach from producing acid
options.D: To treat underlying lung infections directly

explanation: The main goal of endotracheal intubation is to keep the airway open and secure so oxygen can reach the lungs safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: A patient with a severe drug overdose has lost consciousness and normal gag reflexes. Why is intubation urgently required here?

options.A: To protect the lungs from choking on stomach contents
options.B: To reverse the chemical effects of the drug quickly
options.C: To increase blood flow to the brain tissue
options.D: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature

explanation: Unconscious patients lose protective airway reflexes, putting them at high risk of aspirating vomit into their lungs, which intubation prevents. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the name of the special alignment used to help visualize the vocal cords during intubation?
explanation: Placing the patient's head in the sniffing position aligns the oral, pharyngeal, and laryngeal axes for a better view of the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: Why is checking the suction apparatus considered a critical step before beginning the intubation procedure?

options.A: To inflate the balloon cuff once the tube is in the trachea
options.B: To quickly clear vomit, blood, or secretions blocking the view
options.C: To measure the exact volume of air inside the patient's lungs
options.D: To deliver humidified oxygen straight down the breathing tube

explanation: Unforeseen fluids can instantly obscure the clinician's view of the vocal cords, making immediate suction essential for patient safety. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of pre-oxygenating a patient right before intubation?

options.A: To clean out bacteria from the upper respiratory tract
options.B: To relax the vocal cords so the tube slides in easily
options.C: To stimulate a strong cough reflex in the trachea
options.D: To build an oxygen reserve and prevent low blood oxygen

explanation: Pre-oxygenation fills the lungs with pure oxygen to give the healthcare team a safe window of time while securing the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h3)

question: A patient receives a sedative medication right before intubation and suddenly becomes very dizzy with a dangerous drop in blood pressure. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The bag-valve-mask was squeezed too hard during manual ventilation
options.B: The patient was not breathing enough oxygen before the procedure started
options.C: Many induction drugs cause blood vessels to relax and lower blood pressure
options.D: The endotracheal tube was inserted too deeply into the right mainstem bronchus

explanation: Sedatives and induction agents frequently cause vasodilation, which can drop blood pressure sharply, particularly in unstable patients. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h3)

question: What is the maximum recommended time limit for a single intubation attempt to protect the patient?
explanation: Limiting attempts to 30 seconds prevents prolonged interruption of oxygen delivery and avoids severe hypoxia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why must the healthcare team pause and provide manual ventilation between failed intubation attempts?

options.A: To allow the local anesthetic time to numb the vocal cords fully
options.B: To let the mechanical ventilator automatically calibrate itself
options.C: To cool down the laryngoscope light bulb so it does not burn tissue
options.D: To restore the patient's blood oxygen levels before trying again

explanation: Stopping to ventilate the patient prevents dangerous drops in oxygen saturation while the team regroups. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: What is considered the gold standard imaging method for verifying the final position of an endotracheal tube?
explanation: A chest X-ray provides definitive visual proof showing exactly how far the tube is from the tracheal bifurcation (carina). [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h5)

question: A newly intubated patient has absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest and gurgling noises over the epigastrium when ventilated. What does this strongly suggest?

options.A: The ventilator settings are delivering too much volume
options.B: The tube is accidentally placed in the esophagus
options.C: The patient has a sudden blockage in the left bronchus
options.D: The endotracheal tube cuff has leaked completely

explanation: Gurgling over the stomach and lack of breath sounds on the left indicate the tube went down the esophagus instead of the trachea. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why should a nurse measure and document the centimeter depth marking of the endotracheal tube at the patient's lip?

options.A: To find out when the plastic material of the tube needs replacing
options.B: To calculate the exact amount of suction pressure needed daily
options.C: To determine how much air belongs inside the mechanical ventilator
options.D: To quickly notice if the tube slips out or pushes in too deep

explanation: Recording the depth mark allows any nurse to verify at a glance that the tube has not migrated out of position. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is the recommended target range for endotracheal tube cuff pressure to prevent tracheal damage?
explanation: Maintaining cuff pressure between 20 and 30 cmH2O seals the airway adequately without cutting off blood flow to the tracheal lining. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: If an endotracheal tube advances too far down the trachea, which mainstem bronchus does it most commonly enter?

options.C: It stops directly at the carina

explanation: The right main bronchus has a wider and more vertical angle, making it much easier for a deep tube to slip into it by mistake. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: A mechanically ventilated patient suddenly experiences high-pressure alarms, low oxygen saturations, and absent breath sounds on the left side. Which emergency troubleshooting step comes first using the DOPE mnemonic?

options.A: Increase the oxygen concentration on the wall regulator
options.B: Immediately remove the breathing tube completely
options.C: Check for tube displacement or right mainstem intubation
options.D: Administer a dose of rescue bronchodilator medication

explanation: Sudden unilateral breath sound loss points directly to tube displacement, which must be assessed and corrected immediately. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: Why is it important to suction the back of the throat right before removing an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To make it easier to deflate the inner balloon cuff
options.B: To test whether the patient's gag reflex is fully recovered
options.C: To prevent pooling secretions from sliding down into the lungs
options.D: To measure the exact amount of saliva produced during sleep

explanation: Suctioning above the cuff clears out collected saliva and mucus so they do not get aspirated into the trachea as the tube comes out. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h8)
